newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down as stg hits record high vs DMk.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down as stg hits record high vs DMk.

text.p: LIFFE grains came down on Thursday, hit by the renewed post budget strength of sterling.
Sterling/mark broke through a new 5-year high of 2.9470, its highest level since mid-May 1992 as foreign exchange markets bet on higher exchange rates after Wednesday's UK budget.
"The buyers backed off and the market came down," one grains trader said.
Given the size of sterling's rise, some market players had been expecting a bigger fall, and were looking for more weakness, he said.
November was most active, with 297 of a total 578 lots traded. It last changed hands 1.50 stg lower at 84.65 stg.
Old crop came off worse, but on slim volume. July last changed hands at 80.00 stg, 2.00 stg lower, but only 46 lots of July were done.

Physical market grain brokers had little to report. But the few trades they did report showed a similar fall to futures. Feed wheat was done for July delivery to Norfolk/Suffolk at 84.50 stg, compared with 86.00 reported on Wednesday.
